import os
import sys
from click.testing import CliRunner
import click

def test_prompt_backspace_linux(monkeypatch):
    if sys.platform.startswith("linux"):
        runner = CliRunner()

        # Simulate user typing "hello" then backspacing twice to get "hel"
        # and then pressing enter.
        # The bug causes backspace to remove two characters, so "hello\b\b"
        # would result in "he" instead of "hel".
        # The bug also causes the prompt to be deleted when backspacing the entire line.
        # We'll test a simple backspace scenario.
        input_data = "hello\b\b\n"

        # Mock sys.stdin.isatty to ensure we hit the interactive prompt path
        monkeypatch.setattr(sys.stdin, "isatty", lambda: True)

        result = runner.invoke(click.prompt, ["Enter text"], input=input_data)

        # The expected output should be "hel" if backspace works correctly
        assert result.output.strip().endswith("hel")
        assert "hel" in result.output
        assert result.exit_code == 0
        assert result.exception is None

        # Test another scenario: typing "abc" and then backspacing all of it
        # and then typing "def"
        input_data_full_backspace = "abc\b\b\bdef\n"
        result_full_backspace = runner.invoke(click.prompt, ["Enter text"], input=input_data_full_backspace)

        assert result_full_backspace.output.strip().endswith("def")
        assert "def" in result_full_backspace.output
        assert result_full_backspace.exit_code == 0
        assert result_full_backspace.exception is None
